title: Choose the composition of the monthly issue page
question: Same world as the chess view: the osm.sh terminal in daylight. This round is composition only, for the home page that carries this month's puzzle, its answer form, and last month's solution and solvers. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Release notes
options.lineage: a project's CHANGELOG, newest release on top
options.thesis: Each month is a release. The current version heads the page with the puzzle as its notes and one field to reply; the previous version sits beneath it, unfolded into its solution and the people who solved it; older versions run on as headers.
options.viewport: Header rule with puzzles.osm.sh. A version rule ‘── 2026.10 ── October ── open ──’ then the statement in a 68ch prose column (LaTeX set inline, figure or file link below). Directly under it the answer form: ‘> name’ and ‘> answer’ on one command-style line with a submit key. Below, the previous version’s rule ‘── 2026.09 ── solved ──’ with the write-up and a ‘solved by’ column of names and dates. Then the archive as version rules only. Status bar at the bottom with issue, state, and solver count.
options.risk: Reads as software release notes to a friend who does not write software; the version tags must stay dates, not semver.

raised.raise: The page descends chronologically and every issue is signed and dated at its foot: author, publish date, and when its solution unlocked.

options.label: This month | last month
options.lineage: the chess view's before | after split, applied to time
options.thesis: Two panes side by side: this month’s puzzle and its answer form on the left, last month’s solution and solvers on the right. The page is always the present and the past at once.
options.viewport: Header rule. Left pane framed ‘── this month ──’: statement, figure, the name and answer fields, submit. Right pane framed ‘── last month ──’: the solution write-up and the solved-by list. Beneath both, one rule-line row of archive links. Status bar. On mobile the panes stack, this month first.
options.risk: The solution pane competes with the puzzle for attention on desktop, and a long write-up makes the right pane much taller than the left.

options.label: Man page
options.lineage: a Unix manual page, sections in their canonical order
options.thesis: The issue is a manual page: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, FILES, SUBMIT, SOLVERS, SEE ALSO. The puzzle is the DESCRIPTION; last month lives under SEE ALSO as its own page.
options.viewport: Top line ‘PUZZLE(2026.10)’ left and right like a man header. NAME: the puzzle title and a one-line summary. SYNOPSIS: what kind of answer is expected. DESCRIPTION: the statement with LaTeX and figure. FILES: downloads. SUBMIT: name and answer fields. SOLVERS: names in solve order. SEE ALSO: last month’s solution, linked. Footer line with author and date.
options.risk: The strongest terminal fit but the least legible to a non-technical friend, and the previous solution is a click away rather than on the page.

options.label: Sampler sheet
options.lineage: a stitched practice sampler, bands in order, signed and dated at the foot
options.thesis: Issues as bands descending chronologically on one sheet, each signed and dated.
options.viewport: One sheet of monthly bands, newest at top, signature at the foot of each.
options.case: Its chronological descent and signed foot fuse cleanly into the release notes and are donated there; alone it loses on clarity of where to answer.
options.risk: Read literally it becomes decoration over a reading page.

options.label: Cutting bench rail
options.lineage: film cutting bench with a perforated select rail
options.thesis: Sections string along a rail; state is a mark, not a hue.
options.viewport: Issues as frames on a rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: a rail across a reading page fights the prose column.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue: open, solved, and unlocked are words in the rule, never colored badges.

options.label: Cathode gauze
options.thesis: Every value present as a ghost; one struck forward.
options.case: Loses both axes: dark, unframed, and ruleless against a light world built on rules.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.case: Loses both axes: no grid, no rules, no reading column.

options.label: Drawcord cape
options.lineage: silk cape with hidden drawcord channels
options.thesis: One pull transforms a flat plane.
options.case: Loses both axes: a reveal mechanic has nothing to reveal on a reading page.

options.label: Daylight section
options.lineage: architectural section lit by the sun's path
options.case: Loses both axes: no mapping from a puzzle to rooms and apertures.
